# Expected — 09 domain-lookalike-payroll

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | scam |
| Family | Jobs |
| Expected label | **Scam markers: 3 or more** |
| Recovery branch | no |
| Purpose | The authority costume with a typo in it: a borrowed brand, a lookalike domain, bank details by reply — tests the kit's attention to the sender address |

## Markers that MUST appear (each quoted from the message)

| Category | Must quote |
|---|---|
| Authority costume | the borrowed brand — "Zenith Cloud Solutions" worn by "zenith-cloudsolutlons.com" (the `solutlons` with an L) |
| Information extraction | the reply ask — "Bank name / Account number / Routing number" |
| Urgency | "within 3 business days, your payroll will be suspended" |

## Markers that must NOT appear

- Payment shape — no money is sent by the victim in this message; bank details *received* are the take. Do not invent a fee.

## Guards

- The lookalike domain must be shown in the report — the sender line is quoted evidence, and the typo is the detail that carries it. A report that misses the domain entirely fails this fixture even with the right label.
- "Dear employee" — a payroll office that already holds the account details does not know the person's name; this supports the reading and may be noted.
- The verify checklist must include the behavioral rule: never re-confirm bank details by email reply; reach the real company through a channel *you* look up.
